core.title: Tests do not write to shared live state
core.given: Any test code, where test context is defined by the profile as the union of two independent criteria — any code the stack's test runner executes, and any code inside the stack's test-declaration constructs — regardless of file name and regardless of whether the test is new or pre-existing
core.when: The test mutates the shared process environment or writes to the filesystem, for any purpose
core.then: The test MUST NOT mutate the shared process environment nor write to a filesystem path outside a test-owned temp/fixture location (shared live state: anything a later test also sees).
prefer: Scope every write to a temp directory the test owns and cleans up.
Pass configuration explicitly instead of mutating the environment, e.g. construct the code under test with the test's settings handed in directly.
avoid: Mutating the shared process environment from a test — it looks local but is global, and is the most common, least obviously wrong form of pollution.
Writing to repository or other shared filesystem paths that later tests also see.
unless: The write targets a path scoped to a test-owned temp/fixture location (the profile's allowed write scopes).
The operation is a read; only the write family is in scope.
core.why: A polluting test does not fail; it makes a DIFFERENT test fail later, often only under a different order, with the failure pointing at the victim rather than the culprit (displaced failure). That asymmetry is why this is the family's strict rule, matching core: finding one after the fact costs days.
evidence: The stack's discipline check reports no mutations of the shared process environment (the profile's environment-mutation idiom) in test code.
The check reports no write-family filesystem calls whose literal path is outside the allowed test temp/fixture scopes.
Suite passes regardless of test order (no displaced failures).
verification: A static discipline check (validator) scans all test code — existing and changed — where test context is any code the stack's test runner executes or any code inside the stack's test-declaration constructs, whatever the file name. It flags mutations of the shared process environment (the profile's environment-mutation idiom) and write-family filesystem calls whose literal path is not scoped to the profile's allowed test temp/fixture locations.
Reads are never flagged; only the write family is in scope.
A computed (non-literal) path cannot be judged by the static check and is not reported (a check limitation, not a permission).
A diff-level change observer, when present, is only an optimization to surface new violations early; it does not restrict applicability — pre-existing tests are equally in scope.
Severity 4; disposition strict — the rule fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: test (any code the stack's test runner executes, or any code inside the stack's test-declaration constructs, regardless of file name and change status — the profile's test context)
test file by name pattern (non-exhaustive pre-filter; patterns from the profile)
shared-live-state mutation in test code (existing or changed)
write-family filesystem call in test code

fires: Any test assigns to the shared process environment, for whatever purpose (configuration, feature flags, setup, or anything else).
Any test performs a write-family filesystem operation (write, append, directory creation, removal, etc.) with a literal path outside any test-owned temp/fixture location, for whatever purpose.
An existing (unchanged) test already contains such a mutation or write when the suite or file is checked.

Code in scope through either test-context criterion — executed by the test runner or inside the stack's test constructs — is in scope even when its file name matches none of the profile's pre-filter patterns; the patterns are a fast path, not the scope.
doesNotFire: A test only reads files or reads the environment.
A test writes to a path scoped to a test-owned temp/fixture location (the profile's allowed write scopes).
A test writes using a computed (non-literal) path — the static check cannot judge it and does not report it (a check limitation, not a permission).
Production (non-test) code sets environment variables or writes files.

proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: tooling.test_runner names the runner but not which code counts as test code; suffix.* keys are only name patterns (non-exhaustive by this rule's own admission); roles.assignment governs file-to-role assignment in general and cannot express code-level test constructs appearing in any file. The core's test-context concept needs its own key.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's concrete idiom for mutating the shared process environment, which the core forbids in test code and the check flags.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key describes the shared mutable process environment or how code mutates it; idiom.runtime_globals lists framework globals forbidden to inner roles, which is a different concept.

proposedKeys.meaning: Path markers (matched as substrings or globs) that identify test-owned temp/fixture locations where a test may write; writes scoped to them are allowed, every other write target counts as shared live state.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key names writable test-scoped locations: layout.test_location says where test files are placed and idiom.runtime_globals lists forbidden framework globals; neither expresses the temp/fixture write scopes this rule's unless-clause needs.
